summary:
We developed an AI-powered, satellite-based agricultural decision-support platform and mobile application prototype that integrates NASA SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive) satellite data with a custom-trained machine learning model for soil analysis. Using Python, we processed and modeled high-resolution soil moisture data to create an accessible, real-time monitoring and simulation interface.

Our solution directly addresses the lack of affordable, localized satellite-driven agricultural technologies in the Turkish market, where farmers often rely on traditional, guesswork-based irrigation methods that lead to water waste and reduced crop yields. By eliminating the need for costly physical ground sensors, our platform delivers actionable irrigation schedules and early drought warnings directly to users.

This project is crucial for promoting sustainable water resource management, lowering agricultural production costs, and empowering farmers with scientific, data-driven insights in the face of increasing climate variability.
details: The application we developed features a simple and intuitive interface for farmers, providing daily insights and a decision-support mechanism. By utilizing SMAP and other NASA datasets, the system displays 5-day precipitation forecasts alongside root-zone and surface soil moisture levels. Furthermore, an AI model leveraging machine learning was integrated to interpret previous soil analyses. Based on these interpretations, the system offers actionable recommendations on how to correct imbalances in soil data.
